family.note: Template shape (three-argument color-channel clamp-add over a palette range) only loosely matches; this owner takes three independent per-channel deltas, walks a single flat 63-entry run in place, and has no lower-bound (negative) clamp, unlike the template's shared single delta / dual clamp over two separate 16-entry banks.

domain: Adds independent blue/green/red deltas to 63 consecutive BGR555 palette entries starting at 0x05000002, clamping each channel to 31 with no negative-side clamp, writing back in place.
expressed: walks entries 1..63 of BG palette RAM as one flat do-while loop (0x05000002, +2 per entry)
extracts blue/green/red 5-bit fields from each color and adds a separate caller-supplied delta per channel
clamps each channel to a maximum of 31 only (no minimum clamp)
repacks and stores the color back to the same address before advancing
bounded_checks: first candidate used a for(i=0;i<64;...) ascending loop; the reference's cmp/bne back-edge into the load is a do-while with a `!= 63` exit test and 63 iterations (0x05000002..0x05000080), not 64 -- switching to `do { ... } while (i != 63)` fixed the loop shape (bne back-edge, counter compared for equality) but not the byte count.

reference dedicates r5/r6/r7/r8/lr/ip entirely to the six persistent values (pointer, counter, mask, three deltas) and uses r0-r3 purely as scratch inside the loop body, which is why it needs the extra push{r7}/pop{r3}+mov r8,r3 prologue/epilogue pair; both earlier candidates instead let the register allocator park two of the six persistent values in r0/r1 (no push needed), producing a shorter 84-byte function that never touches r8. This is a register-pressure/scratch-demand difference, not a semantic one, and was not resolved by loop-shape or statement-order changes alone.

reading the actual retained assembly directly (games/gs1/asm/080e727c.s) rather than the paraphrase above shows the reference computes `(u32)c << 16` once and derives blue via `>>26` and green via `>>21` from that single shifted value (matching a real CSE across two field reads sharing a subexpression), and computes red via a fresh `c & 31` immediate rather than reusing the shared blue/green mask register; rewriting the candidate to match both of those exactly (shift-once-then-extract for blue/green, a separate literal 31 for red instead of the shared `mask` variable) improved the candidate from 48/73 to 47/63 differing-halfwords/wrong-instructions while staying at the same 84-byte extent -- genuine progress, but the six-persistent-value register-pressure gap (this owner still keeps one delta in a plain low register r7 instead of promoting all three deltas to r8/lr/ip like the reference) remains unresolved.
notes: Owner byte size (98) matches the family entry's target_bytes; owner takes 3 explicit s32 arguments (blue_delta, green_delta, red_delta) rather than the template's single shared delta.

The residual is a register-allocation/scratch-pressure difference (candidate 84 bytes vs reference 98 bytes, missing the r8-preserving prologue/epilogue pair) rather than a control-flow or value-semantics gap; the loop shape, field-extraction subexpression sharing, clamp order, and store-in-place structure now match the reference's actual retained assembly exactly, and only the delta-parameter register promotion differs.

This looks like a source-shape gap worth another attempt (e.g. a source structure that forces all three deltas to be read after enough other low-register values are already live, deliberately exhausting r0-r7 before the deltas are first used) rather than a compiler-internals residual, since no compiler pass or option was found that could not emit the reference shape.
